deviations: Attendance-oversampling weights reconstructed: in barangays with town-hall meetings (att.prop > 0 in data_agg), attendees weighted by att.prop / survey attendance share and non-attendees by (1 - att.prop) / (1 - survey share); weight 1 elsewhere and for respondents with missing attendance. The authors' exact weight formula is not given in the paper.

Anderson (2008) indices: all five-point items (poverty, gap, corruption, equality, discrimination, harassment) reversed (6 - x) so that higher = more agreement, following the paper's literal statement; binary items (cct, femhouse, fempol) kept as coded. Items standardized on the assignment==0 group of each party's municipalities, inverse-covariance weights from the pairwise covariance matrix of standardized items, index averaged over available items and re-standardized on the control group; built separately within each party sample.
Survey sample: respondents with non-missing party-list turnout response (and non-missing city), N = 1081 (paper reports 1,082; one respondent has missing city).
Only point estimates computed; permutation inference not reproduced (not among the requested quantities).
notes: Attempt-1 was exploratory (data inspection, no RESULT lines). Final run: Table 1 via feols(outcome ~ assignment | city) on data_agg (39 barangays; 18 Akbayan, 21 Umalab Ka; San Diego/San Antonio is one row). Table F.1 unweighted LPMs (outcome x100) among respondents who voted, city FE, assignment. Tables C.3/C.4 weighted index regressions with city FE, barangay-clustered SEs. The orientation of the gender items is ambiguous in the paper; the literal 'higher = more agreement' rule was applied and not revised after seeing results. Codebook PDFs in the mount were read for variable definitions.
